tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The goal peg must contain disks in descending size order, with the largest disk at the bottom and the smallest at the top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you compare the current configuration to the goal, ensure the target peg follows this ordering; it guides which disks must be placed before others.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If the goal is all disks on peg 2, the final stack must read [5,4,3,2,1] from bottom to top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place Larger Disks Before Smaller
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Because a larger disk can never sit on a smaller one, any disk that must appear below another in the final stack must be moved onto the goal peg before the smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When planning the move order for a target peg, schedule moves of larger disks first, then place the smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To achieve [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, move disk 4 onto peg 2 before moving disk 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly; you must first relocate those smaller disks to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the desired disk to move is not the topmost on its peg, move the obstructing smaller disks elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 1, first move disks 1, 2, 3 to the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The peg that is neither the current source nor the final target serves as a temporary holding area for smaller disks while larger disks are being moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During a sub‑problem where you need to free a larger disk, move the obstructing smaller disks onto the auxiliary peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: When moving the 4‑disk tower from peg 1 to peg 2, peg 0 is used to store disks 1‑3 temporarily.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Sub‑tower Transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another follows the recursion: move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk to the target, then move the k‑1 disks from auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous block of disks, apply this recursive pattern rather than trying to move each disk individually.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To transfer 4 disks from peg 1 to peg 2, first move 3 disks to peg 0, then move disk 4, then move the 3 disks onto peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg where the top disk (if any) is larger, never onto a smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move, verify both that the source peg’s top disk is the one you intend to move and that the destination peg’s top disk (or empty) is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg whose top is disk 1 is illegal; moving it onto disk 3 or an empty peg is legal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing a move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to confirm that the final arrangement matches the goal exactly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the answer, run through the entire sequence to catch any illegal move or missing disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the 15‑move solution for the 4‑disk transfer and verify that peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering will be parsed incorrectly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the move list, always label pegs with 0‑based indices.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk from peg 1 to peg 2 is written as [disk, 1, 2], not [disk, 2, 3].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date mental (or written) list of the top disk on each peg to quickly decide which moves are possible and legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before each move, consult the current top‑disk list to ensure you are moving the correct disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 to peg 0, the top of peg 0 becomes disk 1, and peg 1’s top becomes disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can treat that peg as the base of the sub‑problem and apply the classic recursion without moving those larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg has some disks that are already in their final positions (typically the largest ones), ignore them and solve the remaining sub‑tower transfer as if the target were empty.
tower-of-hanoi.example: With disk 5 already on peg 2, moving the 4‑disk tower from peg 1 to peg 2 proceeds exactly as a standard 4‑disk transfer, using peg 0 as auxiliary.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets the rule that larger disks cannot rest on smaller ones and may focus only on moving the desired disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the size of the destination peg's top disk (or emptiness) before committing a move; larger must never be placed on smaller.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may track disks incorrectly or assume any disk can be moved once its lower disks are in place.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a clear list of the top disk on each peg and only select moves that involve that top disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to finish the goal quickly by dumping small disks, overlooking that larger disks still need to be placed underneath.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the "Place Larger Disks Before Smaller" principle: schedule larger‑disk moves onto the goal peg before any smaller ones.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model confuses human‑friendly 1‑based numbering with the required 0‑based indexing for the output format.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Remember that pegs are numbered 0, 1, 2 in the answer; double‑check each move's peg numbers before finalising the list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the constructed move list is correct without replaying it, leading to unnoticed errors.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After drafting the moves, simulate them step‑by‑step (or mentally) to ensure the final configuration matches the goal exactly.
